question_text: May Customer transfer perpetual licenses under the Microsoft Customer Agreement? (Variant 1)
draft_gold_answer: Yes, Customer may transfer fully-paid, perpetual licenses to an Affiliate or a third party.

question_text: What license type does Microsoft grant to Customer for Products? (Variant 2)
draft_gold_answer: Microsoft grants Customer a nonexclusive, limited license to use Products ordered.

question_text: Does Customer acquire ownership rights in the Products or software? (Variant 3)
draft_gold_answer: No, Customer receives only limited license rights; Microsoft reserves all other rights.

question_text: What notice period is required for Customer to terminate for convenience? (Variant 4)
draft_gold_answer: Customer may terminate for convenience upon 60 days prior written notice.

question_text: Within how many days must undisputed invoiced fees be paid? (Variant 5)
draft_gold_answer: Customer must pay undisputed amounts within 30 calendar days from invoice date.

question_text: Under what exact condition may perpetual licenses be transferred to an unrelated third party? (Variant 6)
draft_gold_answer: Perpetual licenses may be transferred to a third party solely in connection with the transfer of hardware to which they were assigned.

question_text: If Microsoft terminates an order for non-payment, does Customer receive a pro-rata refund? (Variant 7)
draft_gold_answer: No, in termination for cause by Microsoft, no refunds are provided.

question_text: Can Customer reverse engineer the software if necessary to fix interoperability bugs? (Variant 8)
draft_gold_answer: No, reverse engineering, decompilation, and disassembly are strictly prohibited without exception.

question_text: When does the indemnification defense duty apply to third-party IP claims? (Variant 9)
